judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short release mechanic conditioned on a sale "in accordance with the terms of this Agreement" and on payment of "the agreed amount"; both are determinate by reference elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with Section 4.2's requirement that Lender hold at least $250,000,000 of Eligible Notes Receivable at all times and with Permitted Dispositions clause (e)'s 80%-of-balance floor; neither is mentioned here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three enumerated triggers with a reassignment obligation on Borrower-prepared forms; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Trigger (iii) applies to notes in default, yet the Note Receivable Collateral definition is limited to property securing *Eligible* Notes Receivable, which defaulted notes are not.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The bring-down is stated both "as of the date hereof" and "as of the Closing Date", which the Closing Date definition makes the same day — redundant drafting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.3(a) states the same bring-down and Compliance Certificate paragraphs 2 and 5 duplicate it with a further carve-out for actions permitted by Lender that this chapeau lacks.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[G]ood and indefeasible title" for personalty and "good and marketable title" for realty are different, somewhat archaic standards used in the same sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 7.2's Lien covenant and the Permitted Liens definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (c) is circular (eligible because not excluded by the eligibility definition), and clause (b)'s "without any known defenses" imports an undefined knowledge standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause (i) adds a substantive requirement — a lien on property "on which a commercial or residential development is located or is expected to be built" — that appears nowhere in the Eligible Notes Receivable definition, so the two eligibility tests differ.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[C]ommensurate with forms and documentation used by prudent lenders in the same or similar circumstances" is a vague benchmark, and the third sentence gives an unqualified representation that "all aspects of Borrowers' operations" comply with all laws.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That absolute compliance representation sits against the Section 5 chapeau's "in all material respects" qualifier and against Section 6.10's covenant qualified by Material Adverse Change — three different compliance standards.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[F]it for such purposes" is a soft standard, but the representation is trivial in this transaction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Equipment definition and Permitted Dispositions clause (a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A location representation with a proviso for loan files in a public warehouse; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.15 states the identical proviso as a negative covenant and Section 6.9 governs updates, so the three are aligned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short factual representation; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 6.1's accounting-system covenant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A schedule representation; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 7.5's bar on changing state of organization.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A schedule representation with an update mechanism; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.9 permits the update on 30 days' notice, exactly as cross-referenced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A schedule representation qualified by "if any"; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 7.5's bar on changing those numbers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closing-date snapshot representation; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.4(b) covers claims acquired later; the two dovetail.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trailing parenthetical "(as may be necessary by the applicable laws of such state)" is garbled and adds nothing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.1(e)-(f) and 6.12's existence covenant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out "[o]ther than as described on Schedule 5.8 or in an Offering Circular" hangs the representation on a collectively defined and amendable set of offering documents.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Offering Circular definition covers the operating agreement and subscription agreements "as amended from time to time", so the exception can expand unilaterally after closing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed schedule requirements framed in corporate share terms for entities that may be LLCs; the Stock definition covers that.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Subsidiary definition excludes Bar-K, Inc., New Funds and most post-closing entities, so this "complete and accurate list" may be materially narrower than it appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A negative representation with the same Offering Circular carve-out; determinate in form.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same interaction with the amendable Offering Circular as clause (b); no direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line authorisation representation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 3.1(c)'s resolutions condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four enumerated no-conflict limbs with express carve-outs; conventional and precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.9(c) and 3.1(q).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat no-registration representation with a consents carve-out; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1(q) requires Borrowers to have obtained "all licenses, approvals or evidence of other actions required by any Governmental Authority" in connection with the Loan Documents, which presupposes that some may be required — mild tension with this representation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard enforceability representation with the customary bankruptcy and equity exceptions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 3.1(h)'s opinion condition and Section 8.16's repudiation default.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It represents the Liens are "first priority ... subject only to Permitted Liens", a formulation that is internally in tension since a prior Permitted Lien defeats first priority.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Permitted Liens clause (c) expressly contemplates Schedule P-1 Liens with priority over Lender's Liens (see Section 2.1(b)(ii)), so the "first priority" representation is qualified elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[T]here are no actions, suits, or proceedings pending and served or, to the best knowledge of any Borrower, unserved or threatened" is a tangled construction whose knowledge qualifier's reach is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.3(g) requires notice of proceedings that could result in a Material Adverse Change, consistent with this representation's carve-out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: GAAP representation with the standard unaudited carve-out and a dated no-MAC statement; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplies the baseline date that Section 3.3(d)'s no-MAC condition omits, so read together they work, if imperfectly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line solvency representation resting on the unusually narrow "Solvent" definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is paired with a fraudulent-transfer heading and Section 16.7's Voidable Transfer revival provision, which assume the fuller statutory solvency concept.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A present-tense intent representation; conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 16.7's revival mechanism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat negative representation using two defined terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No covenant elsewhere restricts adopting a Benefit Plan later, a gap but not a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Knowledge-qualified in limbs (a) and (b) but not (c) and (d); the asymmetry is deliberate and visible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 6.13's environmental covenants and Section 11.3(c)'s indemnity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat brokerage representation; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No conflicting provision; Section 11.3 would cover any resulting claim.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[N]ecessary to the conduct of its business" is a soft standard but the schedule requirement is concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.4(c) requires ongoing registration and supplemental schedules for IP, consistent with this representation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[P]eaceful and undisturbed possession" and "leases material to their business" are soft but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 6.11's rent covenant and Section 6.6's lease-compliance covenant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A schedule listing requirement with specified contents; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "[A]s updated from time to time" has no stated notice mechanism, unlike Schedules 5.5 and 5.7(b) which are updated under Section 6.9; and Section 6.12(d) restricts what accounts a Borrower may maintain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The repeated "(taken as a whole)" qualifier and the double negative "not incomplete by omitting to state any fact necessary" make the standard hard to apply cleanly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.14's disclosure-update covenant expressly says notification does not cure a prior untrue statement, which fits this representation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A schedule representation with detail "as is satisfactory to Lender"; determinate at closing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.1(b) permits Indebtedness "set forth on Schedule 5.20", so the schedule does operative work; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A schedule representation with a no-Affiliate assurance; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Approved Title Insurance Company definition allows Lender to add and remove companies, so the schedule and the definition operate together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The duration formula ("so long as any credit hereunder shall be available and until payment in full of the Obligations") uses "and" where the sense may be "or".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7's parallel chapeau reads "until termination of this Agreement and payment in full of the Obligations", a different formulation for the same concept.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short systems covenant; "reasonably may be requested" is bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.6 and 6.2's reporting requirements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reporting table's timing column and item lettering are jumbled, item (h) is an open "such other reports ... as Lender may request", and the clause refers to "the Servicer Account", a capitalised term defined nowhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires signature by an Authorized Person while the Compliance Certificate definition requires the chief financial officer, and Section 8.2(a) makes any breach of Section 6.2 an immediate Event of Default with no cure period despite the reporting ambiguity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Very long; it contains a dropped word ("with 30 days after"), a garbled cross-reference ("Sections 7.16 and 217"), and requires SEC-style reports "if applicable" for a private fund.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires a monthly Compliance Certificate while the Compliance Certificate form (Exhibit C-1) is drafted for signature by an officer of Manager rather than the chief financial officer the definition names, and the annual accountants' certificate is limited to Sections 7.16 and 7.17 only.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A blank placeholder; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.2(a) makes breach of "Sections 6.1, 6.2, 6.3, 6.5 ... 6.15" an immediate Event of Default, but Section 6.15 is "[Intentionally Omitted]" and 6.4 is blank — the default catalogue points at empty sections.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section is numbered "6.3" in the text although Section 6.3 already exists, and a "defend and hold Lender harmless" indemnity is buried inside a collection covenant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.2(a) makes breach of "Section 6.5" an immediate Event of Default, so the mis-numbering matters; the covenant is also expressly "[s]ubject to Section 4.8", which allocates servicing to Servicer.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[N]ecessary or useful in the proper conduct of its business" is a soft but familiar standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.17 and 6.11 on leases.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed tax covenant with an express Permitted Protest carve-out; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 3.1(i), 8.7 and the Permitted Protest definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[N]aming Lender as the sole loss payee ... or additional insured, as appropriate" leaves the choice of endorsement, and who decides, unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.8(c) requires the same endorsements on any separate insurance and Section 3.1(g) makes delivery a closing condition; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise $50,000 adjustment threshold and a clear default/non-default split on the use of proceeds; "staged payment terms reasonably satisfactory to Lender" is the only soft element.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10 lets Lender obtain insurance on a Section 6.8 failure and Section 2.3(b) governs application of proceeds after default; the pieces fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[C]oncurrent in form or contributing in the event of loss" is technical insurance language but has a settled meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 6.8(a)'s endorsement requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso lets Borrower amend "Schedule 5.5 and Schedule 5.7" although the relevant schedule is 5.7(b), and it conditions relocation on delivering a Collateral Access Agreement without saying from whom.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.5 represents that Collateral is not stored with bailees while this covenant contemplates new locations requiring third-party access agreements, and Section 7.15 bars bailee storage outright except for certain loan files.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The double negative ("other than laws ... the non-compliance with which ... could not reasonably be expected to result in a Material Adverse Change") is awkward but the sense is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.3 represents unqualified compliance of "all aspects of Borrowers' operations", a stricter standard than this covenant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short payment covenant with a Permitted Protest carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.17, 6.6 and the Permitted Protest definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumerated separateness covenants run (a), (c), (d) — clause (b) is missing altogether, so an item of the list has dropped out of the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause (d)'s bar on maintaining depository accounts is qualified for Cash Management Accounts and Account-Debtor accounts, which must be read with Sections 2.6(e) and 6.17 on escrow accounts.
